lesson_title: The Missing Middle: Why (x + 5) Squared Is Not x Squared Plus 25
hook_text: Square x plus 5. Half the class writes x squared plus 25. Put x equal to 1 and watch ten marks go missing.
clip_script: The bracket x plus 5, all squared. Tempting answer: x squared plus 25. Test it. Let x be 1. The bracket is 6, and 6 squared is 36. x squared plus 25 gives 26. Ten missing. Where did it go? The little 2 means the bracket times itself: two identical bags, each holding x and 5. Every item meets every item: x squared, 5x, 5x, 25. The two middle meetings stack into 10x. Real answer: x squared plus 10x plus 25. At x equals 1 that is 36. Found the 10. Picture a square tile with side x plus 5: a big square, a small square, and two rectangles in between. The rectangles are the middle term. Leave them out and the floor has holes. First squared, double the product, last squared. Then check with x equals 1.
visual_style: A square tile with side x plus 5 is sliced into four pieces on a whiteboard; the two rectangles glow and slide together into 10x; a wrong answer is struck through in red and the x equals 1 check ticks green.
pacing: A quick trap, one dramatic test, a visual reveal and a clean rule.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and never lose the middle term again.
